That is so impressive. The rate at which ai can produce formalization artifacts is increasing so quickly. I thought the full classification would be a dream on the horizon for many years, but perhaps not.

One place where an artifact might be helpful because there are genuine questions about the correctness of the proof is abc. Even if what ai produced was indecipherable this would still tell us something quite specific and useful. That stands in contrast to most of the other formalization landmark results.

I think the reality is that CFSG will be done certainly within the next few years (and probably a frontier lab could do it within a month). ABC is a different story, people have been thinking about formalising it for a while but there's still no announcement of anything and you can draw your own conclusions from this.

My limited understanding is that abc started as a human formalization effort much like mathlib. Given the scope of the arguments, that is a very steep mountain. If the proof is correct as written, a swarm of agents might be able to drastically shorten the timeline for formalization. In that limited case ai slop might still have some value. If formalization failed at the critical lemma which Peter Scholze identified that could be interesting circumstantial evidence of its own.
If an AI company can just smash through FLT with enough compute, it could do the abc conjecture assuming the proof was complete or nearly so

Ryan Smith said:

If formalization failed at the critical lemma which Peter Scholze identified that could be interesting circumstantial evidence of its own.

My attitude toward AI in math is generally positive, but it does sadden me that even when (1) a full week of intensive dialogue between two experts and the author and (2) a well-supported and expert-driven formalization project (LANA) both come to the same conclusion that Corollary 3.12 doesn't follow from what comes before, some people apparently think that the real clincher will be when we blindly throw a bunch of agents at the problem and the agents come to the same conclusion.

I don’t know much about the pre AI formalization efforts for abc. My understanding is that it was a huge effort that was projected to take a large number of people-years of effort and has no projected timeline as of yet. Was that famous lemma formalized?
The "famous lemma" is Corollary 3.12, and it was the first target of LANA. As I said, they were unable to see how to formalize it. The ball is now in Mochizuki's court.
Thank you that’s really interesting. That does make it seem less likely that throwing frontier models with lots of compute at the problem would change anything.
